title: 𓂋𓄿 𓏌𓅱 𓉐𓂋𓏏𓂻 𓅓 𓉔𓂋𓅱𓇳
titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 17, part 4
part: Spell 17, part 4 — Osiris meets the ba of Ra, and the plea to Khepri (Plate 10)
work: Book of the Dead of Ani
workEn: Book of the Dead of Ani
draftNote: Draft — the hieroglyphs are read from the printed type of Budge's 1895 edition of the papyrus, and the signs and readings are still being checked; expect changes.
source: Papyrus of Ani (British Museum EA 10470), Plate X. Hieroglyphs transcribed from the interlinear text of E. A. W. Budge, The Book of the Dead: The Papyrus of Ani in the British Museum (London, 1895), pp. 41–52; Budge's transliteration and word-by-word English were used to check the reading of the signs and the sense, never for wording. Only the papyrus's own text is given: the passages Budge supplies from other papyri in his appendixes and footnotes are left out. Transliteration in the Leiden convention, with the reed written i; translation made fresh from the Egyptian. Shown left to right; the papyrus is written in columns read from the top down. The line under each word ("say") is the conventional Egyptological classroom pronunciation — a neutral e between consonants; ꜣ and ꜥ as a; w as u or w; ṯ as tj; ḏ as dj; ḫ and ẖ as kh; š as sh — an artificial teaching pronunciation, since the vowels of Egyptian were never written. The grouping of signs within a word follows Budge's type, which regularises the scribe's hand.
about: The fourth part of Spell 17 goes on with the commentary. It explains the statement that ended part 3, 'I am his ba, who is in the midst of the Two Tjafi': Osiris enters Djedu and finds the ba of Ra there, and the two embrace. Ani's scribe then left out a long passage that other papyri have, and his text resumes in the middle of a sentence with the god who seizes the ba and swallows hearts, whom a gloss names as Seth; Ani calls on Khepri to rescue him from the keepers of the places of slaughter, because he is pure. On the papyrus it runs over Plate 10, lines 110 to 121.

sentences.l: Osiris · it-is · entered-he · into · Djedu · found-he · the-ba · there · of · Ra
sentences.i: It is Osiris, when he entered Djedu and found the ba of Ra there.
sentences.n: wsir pw 'it is Osiris' answers the question: a noun with pw is a sentence without a verb. wsir is the eye before the tall seat, with a god. ꜥq·f 'he entered' is the long-necked bird ꜥq (G35) with q as complement, walking legs and ·f: a sḏm·f set after the answer, 'when he entered'. ḏdw 'Djedu' (Busiris) is the djed-pillar written twice, with w and the town sign (Budge: Ṭeṭṭeṭu). gm·n·f 'he found' is the ibis gm with m as complement and the roll, the n of the sḏm·n·f, the completed action, and ·f; line 111 of the papyrus begins with it. bꜣ … n rꜥ 'the ba of Ra' is split by im 'there', which stands next to the verb. bꜣ is the jabiru with the bowl and flame at its foot, a stroke and a god, as in part 3; rꜥ is the god with the sun on his head. Djedu, in the Delta, was the town of Osiris: here the god of the dead meets the ba of the sun.

sentences.i: Then one embraced the other there.
sentences.n: Budge's groups āḥā and en are joined here as ꜥḥꜥ·n, and ḥept and en as ḥpt·n. ꜥḥꜥ·n is the mast ꜥḥꜥ with the roll (the flat sign is coded Y1, as in part 1) and water n: the auxiliary 'then', which opens a narrative sentence and is followed by a sḏm·n·f. ḥpt·n 'embraced' is the wick ḥ, the stool p and t with two arms encircling (coded D32, approximate) and the low sign U15 as classifiers, then the n of the sḏm·n·f. No subject is written after it, and 'one' is supplied; ky 'the other' is ky with two reeds and a seated man, the object. The reading of the clause is not sure: the n after ḥpt could also be the preposition 'to'. The two who meet are Osiris and the ba of Ra.

sentences.l: then-they · came-into-being · as · the-bas · in-the-midst-of · the-Two-Tjafi(?)
sentences.i: Then they came into being as the bas in the midst of the Two Tjafi(?).
sentences.n: Budge's groups āḥā and enu are joined here as ꜥḥꜥ·n·w; his numeral 112 is printed inside enu, after the water n. ꜥḥꜥ·n·w is ꜥḥꜥ·n as in the clause before, with the chick w and a stroke taken as ·w 'they', the subject pronoun of later Egyptian, as in part 2; the reading is not sure. ḫpr 'came into being' is the scarab with r, taken after ꜥḥꜥ·n with a pronoun as the stative, its ending not written. m bꜣw 'as the bas' is the jabiru written as in the line before, with a god and plural strokes. ḥry-ib 'in the midst of' is the face and the heart, here without their strokes. ṯꜣfy is written as in part 3: the small × before the bird (coded Z9) is not read, the bird is coded G47 (approximate), and the short bar after it is coded as a stroke and not read; two gods follow (Budge: T'afi, 'the two Tchafi'). The reading of the name is uncertain. 'They' are Osiris and the ba of Ra, joined: this is the answer to 'I am his ba, who is in the midst of the Two Tjafi'.

morph.gloss: to do, make (lemma iri) · a second word of the same spelling: the particle ir "when, if" at the head of a clause (ir ꜥq·i "when I entered"), here apparently also bringing in a question ("do you know …?") · also "as for" (particle; ir with a noun puts that noun first as the topic)

to be silent, still (verb) · a second word of nearly the same spelling: the particle grt 'now, moreover, indeed' · the particle grt apparently also written ẖrt, with the sign ẖr, after ir and in (reading not sure)
ba, soul; the Ram, the ba-ram of Mendes (noun)

middle, midst (noun; lit. "what is upon the heart"; m ḥry-ib "in the midst of") · also the inside, inner parts (of the body) · also who is in the midst of, who dwells in (nisba epithet after a noun or name; nṯr ꜥꜣ ḥry-ib ꜣbḏw 'the great god who dwells in Abydos')
the Two Tjafi (?), a pair of gods (dual name; reading uncertain; Budge: T'afi, 'the two Tchafi')

sentences.i: As for the bas in the midst of the Two Tjafi(?) —
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir ẖrt bꜣw ḥry-ib ṯꜣfy in red: a new gloss begins. ir 'as for' puts the bas first as the topic, and ẖrt is taken as the particle grt, as in part 3. ṯꜣfy has no gods here, and the two strokes y are printed above the viper. At this point other papyri, among them the papyrus of Nebseni, from which Budge supplies it, have a long passage that Ani's scribe left out (Nebseni's lines 17–52, which fill most of pp. 42–50 of Budge's edition): the rest of this gloss and more of the commentary. On Ani's papyrus no answer follows, and the text goes straight on with the words of the next unit.

sentences.l: … from · god · that · who-seizes · the-ba · who-swallows · hearts · who-lives · on · rottenness
sentences.i: … from that god who seizes the ba, who swallows hearts, who lives on rotting flesh,
sentences.n: Ani's text resumes here in the middle of a sentence: m-ꜥ 'from (the hand of)', the owl over the arm (printed as one ligature, with a small box at the bird's back), depends on something before it that Ani's papyrus does not have, and the translation opens with '…'. nṯr pwy 'that god' has the flag with a god, and pwy, the demonstrative after its noun. Three participles describe him. ṯꜣy 'who seizes', a participle of ṯꜣ 'seize', is the small bird ṯꜣ (coded G47, approximate; it has a mark at its beak like the × of ṯꜣfy) with ꜣ, two reeds y and the low sign U15 (approximate) (Budge: t'ai). bꜣ 'the ba' has a kneeling man raising one arm after it, the sign that writes ·i 'my' and ink 'I': it is taken as a classifier, but bꜣ·i 'my ba' is possible. nsb 'who swallows' is water n, the tongue ns (coded F20, approximate; the type shows a bar bending down into a long tail), the bolt s and the foot b, with w (not read) and the man with hand to mouth (Budge: nesbu). ḥꜣtw 'hearts' is the forepart of a lion ḥꜣt with t and w, the heart sign and plural strokes, the y of ḥꜣty not written. ꜥnḫ m 'who lives on' is the sign of life with n and ḫ. ḥwꜣw 'rotting flesh' is the wick ḥ, the twisted cord wꜣ (V4) with ꜣ and w, and the pustule (Aa2), the classifier of what is diseased or putrid, with plural strokes (Budge: ḥuau); the noun comes from ḥwꜣ 'rot, stink'. A devourer of the dead is a danger the spells of this book often guard against.

to bury (verb; meaning uncertain) · a second word of the same spelling: Sokar, the falcon god of the Memphite cemetery, drawn on a sledge, made one with Osiris (god's name; Budge: Seker) · also skry, the bark of Sokar (?) (noun)

sentences.i: the keeper of the darkness, who is in the bark of Sokar(?).
sentences.n: iry kkw 'the keeper of the darkness' is a noun with the noun it governs, in apposition to 'that god'. iry is the reed, r and two strokes y with a seated man holding a stick across his body (A47) and the roll, as in part 3. kkw 'darkness' is the basket k twice and w, with the night sky (coded N2, approximate; a small ×-like pendant hangs below it) and a stroke. imy 'who is in' is the nisba of m. skry is the bolt s, k and r with two strokes y and, as classifiers, a bark on a sledge (coded P3, approximate; the type shows posts, a small figure and a × at its prow) and a god: taken as the bark of Sokar, the falcon god of the Memphite cemetery, whose bark on its sledge was drawn round in his festival (Budge: Sekeri, 'the seker boat'). The reading is not sure: the group may also be the god Sokar himself, 'who is in Sokar'.

not; negates the verb ('I have not …') · also in n wn "there is not" · a second word of the same spelling: the preposition "to, for" (n·i "to me") · the negative also before a noun, 'without, there being no …'

failing, harm, fault (?) (noun; perhaps a writing of bꜣgi 'be weary, slack'; Budge: beḳa, 'defect') · perhaps also weariness, inertness (?) (noun; imyw bgꜣ 'those who are in weariness')

sentences.i: Those who are in weariness(?) are afraid of him.
sentences.n: Budge's group senṭ-nef is split here into snḏ and n·f. snḏ 'fear' is the plucked goose snḏ (G54) with a kneeling man raising an arm: a sḏm·f with its subject after it, imyw bgꜣ. n·f 'for him, of him' is water n and ·f; snḏ n 'be afraid of' names what is feared. imyw 'those who are in' is the plural nisba, with a stroke. bgꜣ is written as in part 3, the foot b, the jar-stand g (coded W11, approximate; Budge's numeral 115 is printed after it), ꜣ, then a squatting wrapped man (coded A7, approximate), the classifier of weariness, the bird of bad things and plural strokes (Budge: beḳa). The weary man suggests the sense 'weariness, inertness', perhaps from bꜣgi 'be weary, slack', a word used of the dead; the reading is not sure. Even the dead fear the devourer.

sentences.n: swty 'Seth' is the plant sw with w as complement, t and two strokes y, with a god: Seth's name in the form Suty (Budge: Suti); in part 2 it is written stẖ. A noun with pw makes the answer, 'it is …'. Seth, the murderer of Osiris, is named here as the devourer.

sentences.l: another · saying · the-Great-Wild-Bull(?) · the-ba · of · Geb
sentences.i: Another saying: it is the Great Wild Bull(?), the ba of Geb.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red. Budge's groups Smam and ur are joined here as one name, smꜣ-wr 'the Great Wild Bull' (?): the bolt s, then the vulture ꜣ with a hooked sign at its back read as the sickle mꜣ (U1, approximate; the reading of this pair is uncertain), the owl m as complement, a bull (E1) and a god, then the swallow wr 'great' with r (Budge: Smam-ur). smꜣ with the bull is the wild bull. 'It is' is supplied. bꜣ n gb 'the ba of Geb': Geb is the goose gb with b and a god, the god of the earth (Budge: Seb); line 116 begins with bꜣ. The second gloss gives the devourer another name, as the ba of the earth god.

sentences.l: O · Khepri · in-the-midst-of · bark-his · the-primeval-gods(?) · body-his
sentences.i: O Khepri in the midst of his bark, whose body is the primeval gods(?),
sentences.n: Ani now speaks to the sun-god. i 'O' is the reed with the man raising a hand before his face. ḫpri 'Khepri' is the scarab with r and i and a god; the thin broken lines on either side of the reed are coded as strokes and not read (the right one may be a flaw in the print). ḥry-ib wiꜣ·f 'in the midst of his bark': ḥry-ib has no strokes; wiꜣ is w, i and ꜣ with a boat (coded P1, approximate), and ·f. pꜣwt is the flying pintail pꜣ (G40) with ꜣ, w and t, and two small round loaves (coded X6, approximate) as classifiers: taken as pꜣwt, the primeval gods (Budge: paut, which he renders as the double company of the gods, taking the two loaves for 'two'). pꜣwt ḏt·f is a noun beside a noun, a sentence without a verb, 'the primeval gods are his body', here as a description of Khepri, 'whose body is …'. ḏt 'body' is the cobra ḏ and t with a stroke, and ·f; the cobra's tail runs down beside the t. The reading of pꜣwt is doubtful: Budge's paut is also his reading of psḏt, the Ennead, which part 1 writes otherwise. If the reading is right, Khepri, the sun at dawn, holds the first gods in his own body.

sentences.l: may-rescue-you · the-Osiris · Ani · true-of-voice · from · those · (these) · keepers · who-inspect · has-set · them · the-Lord-to-the-Limit
sentences.i: may you rescue the Osiris Ani, true of voice, from those keepers who inspect, whom the Lord to the Limit has set
sentences.n: The papyrus writes nḥm·k wsir in red, then Ani's name and mꜣꜥ-ḫrw in black, then m-ꜥ nnw pw iryw sipw rdi·n sn in red; nb-r-ḏr is in black. nḥm·k 'may you rescue' is water n, a bowl with spikes along its rim (coded W10, approximate), the sign ḥm of nḥm, and the owl m, printed as the owl-and-arm ligature, so that an arm stands in the word though no ꜥ is read; then ·k, 'you', Khepri: a sḏm·f that asks for what it names. wsir is the low seat (Q2, approximate) and the eye, with no god. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is written short, the plinth and the oar, with no sickle. m-ꜥ 'from' as in line 113. nnw 'those' is the demonstrative as in part 3 (U19 approximate), with a stroke; pw after it is taken as a second demonstrative and is not translated apart. iryw 'keepers' is iry as in line 114 with a stroke for the plural. sipw is the bolt s, i, p and w with the roll, a seated man and a stroke: taken as the plural participle of sip 'inspect, check', 'who inspect', the man marking persons (Budge: sàpu). rdi·n sn nb-r-ḏr 'the Lord to the Limit has set them': Budge's groups erṭā and en are joined here as rdi·n, r and the giving arm with the n of the sḏm·n·f. sn 'them' is the dependent pronoun, the bolt s, n and plural strokes, the object of the verb; as dependent pronouns do, it stands before the noun subject, nb-r-ḏr 'the Lord to the Limit'. The clause describes the keepers; what he set them to do follows in the next unit. Taking rdi alone as a relative form with n·sn 'to them' would leave what he gave unwritten. Budge's numeral 118 is printed inside nb-r-ḏr, after the r. The keepers are the creator's guards in the world below.

sentences.l: to · be-useful · to-him · to · do · the-guarding · of-enemies-his · who-make · slaughter · in · the-places-of-slaughter(?) · who · come-forth · from · guarding-their
sentences.i: to serve him and to keep his enemies under guard, who do slaughter in the places of slaughter(?), who come forth from their custody(?).
sentences.n: Budge's group χu-nef is split here into ꜣḫ and n·f. r ꜣḫ n·f 'to be useful to him' is r with the infinitive: the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ and the roll, and n·f, 'him' being the Lord to the Limit. Budge reads the ibis as χu and renders 'protect'; ꜣḫ n 'be of use to, serve' fits the signs. r irt sꜣwt ḫftyw·f 'to do the guarding of his enemies': irt is the eye ir with t, the infinitive of iri 'do'; sꜣwt is the seated man holding a stick (A47), the sign sꜣ 'guard', with ꜣ, t and w (the w written after the t), the low sign U15 and plural strokes (Budge: satu), the noun 'guard, custody'; ḫftyw·f is written with ꜣ, not read, and a kneeling man (coded A14, approximate), as in part 3. ddyw 'who make' is the giving arm twice, two reeds and w: the plural imperfective participle of rdi, 'give, make', with its doubled stem dd, as in Spell 1, the keepers most likely being its subject. šꜥd 'slaughter' is the pool š (approximate), the arm ꜥ and the hand d with a thorn (coded M44, approximate), the knife and U15 as classifiers: the infinitive of šꜥd 'cut', 'to make cutting'. iꜣt is the reed, ꜣ, t and two strokes with a leg crossed by a knife (D57), the classifier of cutting off, and the house sign: taken as a place of slaughter (Budge: àati), a doubtful reading. nty 'who' is n, t and two strokes, with ꜣ (not read), a seated man and a stroke; pr 'come forth' is the house pr with r and walking legs, taken as the stative after nty, its ending not written. The papyrus has nty pr m sꜣwt·sn, 'who come forth from their guard', translated as it stands, though it sits awkwardly with the keepers' task; with a negative n after nty, which the scribe may have left out, it would read 'from whose guard there is no coming out'. Neither reading is sure. sꜣwt·sn 'their guard' as above, with ·sn, the keepers.

sentences.n: n 'not' is the arms of negation (printed as a line with a raised loop in the middle; coded D35, approximate) with water n. n with a sḏm·f says that something does not or cannot happen: n hꜣb·sn 'they cannot send'. sentences.i: I do not grow weary within their places of killing(?);
sentences.n: n wrd·n·i: n with a sḏm·n·f, 'I do not' (a general statement). wrd 'be weary, still' is the swallow wr with r and the hand d, with the squatting wrapped man (coded A7, approximate) and the bird of bad things, then the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i (Budge: urṭ-nà). sentences.l: not · can-be-done · to-me · thing · of · those · (that-are) · the-abomination · of-the-gods
sentences.i: nothing of those things that the gods abominate can be done to me,
sentences.n: Budge's group àritu-nà is split here into ir·tw and n·i. n ir·tw: n with the passive sḏm·tw·f of iri 'do', the eye ir with t and w: 'it cannot be done'. n·i 'to me' is water n and ·i; Budge renders 'by me', but n names the one something is done to, not the doer. ḫt 'thing' is the placenta ḫ and t with the roll, a stroke and a seated man (A1; the type may be the god-shaped figure). m nnw 'of those': nnw as in line 117, here with the bird of bad things (U19 approximate). bwt 'the abomination' is the foot b, w and t, with the bird of bad things and plural strokes: what is taboo, set beside nnw, 'those (which are) the abomination of the gods'. nṯrw is the flag three times. 'Not … a thing' is put into English as 'nothing'.

sentences.i: because I am a pure one in the midst of the Meseqet.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes the whole clause in red. ḥr-ntt 'because' as in part 3, with its second t not written. ink wꜥb 'I am a pure one': the independent pronoun ink, the pot in and the basket k with a seated man, and a noun after it, a sentence without a verb. wꜥb is the vase pouring water over a leg (D60, approximate; the type shows a dotted arc of water) with the three water lines. In ḥry-ib, the heart and the stroke under it are Budge's restoration of damage, inside his square brackets (Budge: ḥer [àb]). msqt 'the Meseqet' is the three skins ms with s, q and t, and the house sign (Budge: Mesqet); it is a place in the world below, its name of uncertain meaning. Purity is the dead man's claim to pass unharmed.

glossary.imy: imy — who/which is in (the nisba of m "in"; plural imyw)
glossary.skr: skr — to bury (verb; meaning uncertain) · a second word of the same spelling: Sokar, the falcon god of the Memphite cemetery, drawn on a sledge, made one with Osiris (god's name; Budge: Seker) · also skry, the bark of Sokar (?) (noun)
glossary.snḏ: snḏ — to fear, be afraid (verb 3-lit); fear, dread (noun m.; ꜥꜣ snḏ 'great of dread')
glossary.n: n — not; negates the verb ('I have not …') · also in n wn "there is not" · a second word of the same spelling: the preposition "to, for" (n·i "to me") · the negative also before a noun, 'without, there being no …'
glossary.bgꜣ: bgꜣ — failing, harm, fault (?) (noun; perhaps a writing of bꜣgi 'be weary, slack'; Budge: beḳa, 'defect') · perhaps also weariness, inertness (?) (noun; imyw bgꜣ 'those who are in weariness')
glossary.stẖ: stẖ — Seth, god of storm and disorder, who murdered Osiris (god's name; written stẖ or swt; Budge: Sut)
glossary.ḏd: ḏd — to say, speak (verb; ḏd in N "said by N", the formula that brings in a speech); ḏdt "words, speech" (noun from it)
glossary.smꜣ-wr: smꜣ-wr — Sema-wer, 'the Great Wild Bull' (?), a god called the ba of Geb (god's name; smꜣ 'wild bull' + wr 'great'; Budge: Smam-ur)
glossary.gb: gb — Geb, god of the earth (god's name; Budge: Seb)
glossary.i: i — O!, hail (the vocative interjection that opens each declaration)
glossary.ḫpri: ḫpri — Khepri, 'he who comes into being', the sun-god at dawn, shown as a scarab (god's name; from ḫpr 'come into being'; Budge: χeperà)
glossary.wiꜣ: wiꜣ — boat, bark, especially of a god (noun)
glossary.pꜣwt: pꜣwt — the primeval gods (?) (noun f.; Budge: paut)
glossary.ḏt: ḏt — everlastingness, time as unchanging permanence (noun f.; paired with nḥḥ) · a second word of the same spelling: body, person (noun f.)
glossary.nḥm: nḥm — to take away, carry off, snatch · also to rescue, save (from)
glossary.·k: ·k — you, your (2nd person masculine singular suffix pronoun; the basket sign)
glossary.ꜣny: ꜣny — Ani, royal scribe of Thebes, for whom the papyrus was made (personal name)
glossary.mꜣꜥ-ḫrw: mꜣꜥ-ḫrw — true of voice, vindicated (epithet; said of the dead whose words were found true at the judgement) · also, as a noun, vindication, the being found true (m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'in vindication'; written in full or short)
glossary.nn: nn — not, there is not (negative particle; nn + noun 'there is no …'; nn + sḏm·f 'will not …', the negative of the future; nn with a sentence without a verb 'there is not, … is not') · a second word of the same spelling: these, those (demonstrative pronoun before its noun, in classical Egyptian joined to it by the genitive n, nn n X; in later texts also without it) · the demonstrative also written nnw; perhaps also standing first in a sentence without a verb, 'this is …' (?)
glossary.sip: sip — to inspect, check, examine (verb; Budge: sàpu)
glossary.rdi: rdi — to give, put, place; with a sḏm·f, to cause, let (verb; di·f pr·i "he let me come forth")
glossary.sn: sn — two (numeral; sp sn 'twice', written after a word to be said twice) · a second word of the same spelling: brother; companion, fellow (noun m.) · a third word of the same spelling: them, they (3rd person plural dependent pronoun; object of a verb, or subject after a particle)
glossary.nb-r-ḏr: nb-r-ḏr — 'the Lord to the Limit', the Lord of All, a name of the creator god (god's name; Budge: Neb-er-tcher)
glossary.ꜣḫ: ꜣḫ — spirit, the glorified and effective dead (noun; written with the crested ibis) · also glory, effective power (noun m.) · also glorious, effective (adjective) · also to be glorious, be effective, be an effective spirit (verb) · also ꜣḫt, what is effective or useful, a benefit (noun f.) · also ꜣḫ n, to be of use to, serve, benefit (someone) (verb)
glossary.sꜣwt: sꜣwt — Asyut (Lycopolis) · a second word of the same spelling: guard, watch, custody (noun f.; from sꜣw 'guard, keep watch over'; Budge: satu, saut)
glossary.šꜥd: šꜥd — to cut, cut off (verb; infinitive šꜥd 'a cutting')
glossary.iꜣt: iꜣt — standard, the pole or perch carrying a god's emblem; mound (noun) · a second word of the same spelling: a place of slaughter (?) (noun f.; Budge: àati, 'slaughter-houses')
glossary.nty: nty — who, which, that (relative adjective); as a noun "he who"
glossary.pri: pri — to go out, come forth (verb)
glossary.·sn: ·sn — they, them, their (3rd person plural suffix pronoun)
glossary.hꜣb: hꜣb — to be harmed, suffer loss (?) (verb; not otherwise known in this sense, and not hꜣb 'send'; reading and meaning uncertain; Budge: hab) · a second word of the same spelling: to send, send out (verb; Budge: habi, 'made to depart')
glossary.ds: ds — flint; flint knife (noun) · a second word of the same spelling: jug, jar (noun; written with the small jar)
glossary.·i: ·i — I, me (1st-person singular suffix pronoun; the seated-man sign)
glossary.wrd: wrd — to be weary, tired (verb); wrd-ib 'Weary of heart', a name of the dead Osiris (Budge: urṭ; reading doubtful here)
glossary.ẖnw: ẖnw — the inside, interior, residence (noun; m ẖnw 'within')
glossary.smꜣ: smꜣ — to slay, kill · also smꜣwt, place of killing (?) (noun f.; Budge: samatu)
glossary.sḏm·tw·f: sḏm·tw·f — the tw of the sḏm·tw·f, the passive or impersonal form ("one …", "… is done") (verb form; written after the verb, before its suffix)
glossary.ḫt: ḫt — thing, things, property (noun) · a second word of the same spelling: wood, tree, stick, a wooden board (noun m.) · a third word: stairway, terrace (?) (noun; written with the stairway sign; Budge: χet, 'steps') · a fourth word: rear, following (noun; m-ḫt 'after', imyw-ḫt 'those in the following of')
glossary.bwt: bwt — abomination, what is taboo, what one detests (noun f.)
glossary.ḥr-ntt: ḥr-ntt — because (conjunction: ḥr 'on account of' + ntt 'that')
glossary.ink: ink — I (1st person singular independent pronoun; ink N "I am N")
glossary.wꜥb: wꜥb — to be pure, clean; to purify oneself, bathe (verb); pure (adjective) · also wꜥb 'wab-priest', the 'pure one', a priest of the ordinary rank (noun) · also wꜥb 'purification, purity' (noun) · also wꜥbt 'the pure place', the place of embalming (noun f.)
glossary.msqt: msqt — the Meseqet, a place in the world below (place name; meaning of the name not clear; Budge: Mesqet)
